title: Skybase's agent type is visible in its primitive activation states: Prime Transformation Completed, Executor Transformation Inactive
content:
A.6.1.1.4.2.1.2.3.1.1.1 states plainly that "Skybase is a Prime Agent." The surrounding status documents corroborate it structurally: the Prime Transformation Primitive's Global Activation Status is `Completed` (A.6.1.1.4.2.1.2.1.1) with a Single Instance Configuration Document, while the Executor Transformation Primitive's status is `Inactive` (A.6.1.1.4.2.1.3.1.1) with no Instances at all in its Active or Completed directories.

Both transformation primitives exist in every Agent's tree, but only one can ever have run — each is "deployed solely for the one-time transformation of the Agent." Agent type is therefore not a free-text attribute; it is the observable residue of which single-shot primitive was Invoked.

This matters for verification. A reader auditing an Agent's classification does not have to trust the declarative parameter, because a contradictory pair of activation statuses would be visible immediately. The redundancy is deliberate design in a document tree that is otherwise ruthless about not repeating itself.

It also means `Inactive` carries real information here: it marks a capability that structurally exists for uniformity but is foreclosed for this Agent, not one that is merely awaiting use.
description: The two transformation paths are mutually exclusive, so an Agent's classification can be read off status documents rather than taken from a label.
